chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Which of the two is superior, Al-Iman or Al-Islam, for those in front of us say that Al-Islam is superior to Al-Iman?' He said, 'Al-Iman is higher than Al-Islam.' I said, 'So renew that (explanation) for me.' He said, 'What do you say regarding the one who deliberately urinates or defecates in the Sacred Masjid?' I said, 'He would be lashed intensely.' He said, 'Correct.' He said, 'So what do you say regarding the one who urinates or defecates deliberately in the Kabah?' I said, 'He would be killed.' He said, 'Correct. Do you not see that the Kabah is superior to the Masjid, and that the Kabah is included in the Masjid and the Masjid is not included in the Kabah, and similar to that, Al-Iman includes Al-Islam, but Al-Islam does not include Al-Iman.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Imán and Islám according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ontological hierarchy between Iman and Islam, asserting that Iman is the superior, encompassing reality while Islam is its external manifestation. He employs a juridical analogy regarding the severity of punishment for deliberate urination in the Ka'bah versus the broader Masjid to demonstrate that the specific (Ka'bah/Iman) holds greater sanctity and comprehensiveness than the general (Masjid/Islam). This distinction is pivotal in Shia theology for understanding how one can possess Islam without full Iman, but not vice versa.
